nameStory: The Lesser Black-backed Gull gets its name from the dark slate-gray to blackish coloring on its back and wings, which is darker than many other gulls but lighter than its cousin, the Great Black-backed Gull. The "lesser" part distinguishes it as the smaller of the two black-backed species, though it's still quite a substantial bird!
description: The Lesser Black-backed Gull is a large, handsome seabird with distinctive dark gray to blackish wings and back contrasting sharply with its bright white head, chest, and belly. These gulls are about the size of a Herring Gull, with long wings and a sturdy yellow bill. Originally visitors from Europe, they've become increasingly common along New England's coast, especially during winter months, though some can now be spotted year-round.

idTips.label: Dark back and wings
idTips.description: The back and upper wings are distinctively dark slate-gray to blackish, much darker than a Herring Gull's pale gray back, creating a striking contrast with the white body

idTips.label: Yellow legs and bill
idTips.description: Bright yellow-orange legs and a yellow bill with a reddish spot near the tip - the legs are noticeably more yellow than pink, unlike many other large gulls

idTips.label: Wing pattern in flight
idTips.description: Flying birds show dark wings with white trailing edges and distinctive white patches near the wingtips, creating a bold black-and-white pattern against the sky

idTips.label: Size and build
idTips.description: Large and sturdy like a Herring Gull but often appears slightly more streamlined, with a proportionally smaller head and longer wings

idTips.label: Voice
idTips.description: Deep, harsh calls similar to other large gulls - a throaty "kyow-kyow-kyow" that carries well over crashing waves and wind

habitat: Look for Lesser Black-backed Gulls along New England's rocky coastlines, sandy beaches, and harbors, especially around fishing ports and piers where they scavenge for scraps. They're often found mixed in with flocks of Herring Gulls and Great Black-backed Gulls at landfills, parking lots near the coast, and large bodies of water including coastal ponds and estuaries.

seasonality.spring: Numbers begin increasing in late spring as more birds arrive from wintering areas further south. Adults show crisp breeding plumage with bright white heads and vivid yellow bills.
seasonality.summer: Present but less common than in winter, with some non-breeding birds remaining along the coast. Young birds from the previous year may show mottled brown plumage mixed with adult features.
seasonality.fall: Migration brings increasing numbers back to New England waters, with mixed flocks of adults and younger birds in various stages of molt showing patchy plumage.
seasonality.winter: Peak abundance occurs during winter months when large numbers arrive from European breeding grounds, often forming substantial flocks at favorite feeding spots along the coast.

funFact: These gulls are incredible ocean crossers - many of the Lesser Black-backed Gulls you see in New England actually hatched on rooftops and clifftops in places like Iceland, Scotland, or Norway, then flew thousands of miles across the Atlantic Ocean to spend their winter vacation on our shores!
confusionNotes: Most easily confused with the Great Black-backed Gull, but Lesser Black-backeds are noticeably smaller with more slate-gray (rather than jet-black) backs and yellow legs instead of pinkish ones. Memory trick: "Lesser" means smaller size and lighter (less black) back color - two "L"s for Lesser!
contextualKnowledge: This species represents a fascinating example of range expansion in real time - what was once a rare vagrant from Europe has become a regular part of New England's coastal bird community, likely due to climate change and changing ocean conditions affecting their food sources and migration patterns.
compareHints: Among the large white-headed gulls, Lesser Black-backed Gulls are distinguished by their uniquely dark backs - darker than Herring Gulls but not as massive as Great Black-backed Gulls. Their yellow legs set them apart from both Herring Gulls (which have pink legs) and Great Black-backed Gulls (which have pinkish legs and are much larger overall). Ring-billed Gulls are much smaller with paler backs and distinctive black rings around their bills.

relatedSpecies.distinction: Among New England's large gulls, American Herring Gulls are the 'Goldilocks' species - not as massive as Great Black-backed Gulls, not as small as Ring-billed Gulls, but just right in the middle.
Ring-billed Gulls are smaller and more delicate than Herring Gulls, lacking the Herring Gull's robust build and pink legs.

Among New England gulls, Great Black-backed Gulls dwarf the common Herring Gull in size and have much darker backs, while Ring-billed Gulls are significantly smaller with lighter grey backs and distinctive black rings around their bills.
Among New England's large gulls, Iceland Gulls are unique for their combination of medium size and extremely pale wing tips.
Among New England's large gulls, Glaucous Gulls stand out for their pale wingtips—Herring Gulls and Great Black-backed Gulls both have bold black wingtips, while Ring-billed Gulls are much smaller.
Common Gulls are smaller and more delicate than Herring Gulls, with yellow-green (not orange-red) bills and legs, plus a gentler facial expression.
Compared to the common Herring Gull, the Slaty-backed Gull has a noticeably darker slate-gray back and is generally larger and more robust.
Unlike Ring-billed Gulls which have a black ring on a yellow bill, Black-tailed Gulls have a red spot and often a black band near the bill tip.
Compared to the common Ring-billed Gull, Short-billed Gulls are smaller with cleaner wing tips and lack any dark markings on the bill.
Among the large white-headed gulls in its genus, the California Gull is most similar to the Ring-billed and Herring Gulls but sits between them in size.
Unlike the common white-bodied gulls of New England like Herring and Ring-billed Gulls, Heermann's Gull has the reverse color scheme with a dark body and white head.
